headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad networked API use can leak or misapply outputs, while the pair has no shared-channel evidence to justify stronger injection claims.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between data-engineering-zoomcamp and RD-Agent, and the course repo is not runnable. RD-Agent can run browsers, but there is no evidence it ingests the course’s outputs by default. This makes a prompt-injection pathway unproven rather than merely unlikely.
conditions: IF an orchestrator pipes data-engineering-zoomcamp text directly into RD-Agent prompts, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the two, attacker-controlled content could cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any automatic prompt chaining between outputs and inputs.
Require explicit human review before copying text from one agent to the other.
Add provenance labels to any transferred artifacts.
requires-engineering: introduce content-sanitization and allowlist parsing for inter-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, papers, execution traces, logs, and requests API keys, while data-engineering-zoomcamp is a course repo with no declared data classes. The pairwise leakage path is mainly through RD-Agent’s broad network egress and API calls; the course agent does not add a documented leak sink, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at sensitive local files, RD-Agent may transmit them through external APIs.
IF both agents share a workspace containing secrets or reports, RD-Agent can expose them via logs or API calls.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared workspace.
Run RD-Agent with least-privilege API keys.
Separate course materials from research data directories.
Review and redact logs before sharing them.
requires-engineering: add egress filtering and secret-scanning on outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: data-engineering-zoomcamp has no documented write or network surfaces, while RD-Agent supports multiple instances and broad API use. Because the first agent is not runnable and no shared mutable resource is documented, direct write conflict is not established; the remaining risk is limited to unusual orchestration choices.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted onto the same writable directory, file contention becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same API credentials, they may race on shared quotas or state.
mitigations: Use separate output directories.
Assign distinct credentials per agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo or log path.
Serialize any shared-resource access.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is an automation-oriented research agent that can act on outputs via APIs and browser use, while data-engineering-zoomcamp is a course artifact that could be treated as source material. There is no direct evidence of a verification step between them, so if RD-Agent consumes the course’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports.
conditions: IF RD-Agent ingests text from data-engineering-zoomcamp without verification, it may propagate mistakes.
IF RD-Agent uses the course output to generate reports or API-driven actions, the error can cascade downstream.
mitigations: Require source citations for any transferred claim.
Insert a human review step before actions.
Compare outputs against an independent reference.
Limit RD-Agent to draft-only mode for imported content.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, logs, and multiple external APIs, which can create retention and residency obligations; data-engineering-zoomcamp is a public course repo and does not itself add a compliance burden. The mismatch is therefore driven by RD-Agent’s documented data classes and egress, not by the course agent, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated reports are processed by RD-Agent, residency and retention controls must be checked.
IF logs from RD-Agent are retained alongside course materials, deletion/export handling may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent runs.
Set short log-retention windows.
Document the data-processing purpose.
Review vendor/API terms for residency.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention and deletion workflows.
